errors.description: The model incorrectly reconstructed the arrow’s trajectory order. According to the Scene Description, the arrow moves from white → orange → yellow, not white → yellow → orange. This fundamental misordering of events led the model to analyze the wrong segment (white-to-yellow) as the first leg and incorrectly conclude yellow was reached in the shortest time. The error stems from misperceiving or misremembering the visual sequence of the arrow’s path.

errors.description: The model introduced an unjustified assumption — that speed was constant — to justify using visual path length as a proxy for time. While this might be a reasonable heuristic in ambiguous cases, the video explicitly provided timing data (e.g., 0.50s for white-to-orange), which the model ignored. This led to a flawed reasoning chain based on visual estimation rather than using the available temporal evidence.

analysis_result.analysis: The model failed primarily due to misordering the sequence of the arrow’s movement — it incorrectly assumed the path was white → yellow → orange, whereas the correct sequence was white → orange → yellow. This led to analyzing the wrong segment (white-to-yellow) as the shortest time leg, when in fact the white-to-orange segment (0.50s) was shortest. The model compounded this error by relying on visual distance estimation under a constant-speed assumption, ignoring the explicit timing cues embedded in the video. The failure is rooted in temporal misordering and an unjustified heuristic, not a perceptual misidentification of colors or shapes.
